thread.title: Stocks Soar Because It Was Never Really About the Shutdown

author: Barron's
title: Stocks Soar Because It Was Never Really About the Shutdown
text:
Stocks are bouncing back in a big way after the Senate reached a short-term deal to re-open the government .
Bloomberg News The S&P 500 has gained 0.5% to 2,824.49 at 12:39 p.m. today, while the Dow Jones Industrial Average has risen 82.20 points, or 0.3%, to 26,153.92. The Nasdaq Composite has climbed 0.7% to 7,388.37.
As Barron's Randall W. Forsyth noted on Friday evening, "while the wrangling occupied Washington insiders (and the news), outside the Beltway a government shutdown seemed rather remote ." So remote in fact, that the stock market ignored it, for the most part, and one Barron's columnist--OK, me--argued that last Friday's drop was more about bond yields than the potential shutdown. Yes, it could tamp down investor enthusiasm for stocks, but not knock the market down. That's not just true of this shutdown, but most of them . "Recent government shutdowns have not elicited a significant response from financial markets," BofA Merrill Lynch economists Michelle Meyer and Joseph Song wrote in a report this morning.
And with the shutdown over, at least temporarily, the stock market can get back to doing what it's done since the start of the year: rally.
Stocks We're Watching There were only two major earnings releases this morning, but both were greeted with elation by investors. Wynn Resorts ( WYNN ) has gained 6.7% to $191.63 at 12:48 p.m. today after releasing numbers so good its boosted other casino stocks too . Halliburton ( HAL ), meanwhile, has risen 4.7% to $55.52 after releasing earnings so good that Guggenheim upgraded the stock . Over in research land, Deutsche Bank's analysts found glimmers of hope at Snap ( SNAP ), Apple ( AAPL ) got downgraded at Atlantic Equities, and Soctiabank touted Verizon's potential .
Barron's Tiernan Ray took a deep dive into RISC-V , the name of a non-profit foundation founded by U.C. Berkeley professor David Patterson to create one single "instruction set architecture" that can be used across all manner of chips.
And yes, bitcoin got creamed .
Grocers Bounce Back from the Amazon Apocalypse Bloomberg News Amazon.com ( AMZN ) opened its first cashier-free store today --hooray!--but the retailer may be less of a threat to grocery stores than it first appeared following its purchase of Whole Foods .
At the time, there was plenty of worry that it would take over the grocery space , as it has done in so many other areas of retail . But now it seems that fears of the grocery apocalypse may have been overblown, say Stifel analyst Christopher Growe and his team. Growe writes that there are a number of grocery categories that are benefiting from online growth, from pet supplies to vitamins and beauty, but that shopping intentions at Whole Foods are "largely unchanged" since Amazon's purchase of the chain, according to his research and Stifel's consumer spending survey. As such, Growe writes that he maintains his belief that "Amazon's ultimate effect on the industry is being over-estimated."
That's an an attitude that's becoming more prevalent among other analysts as well, writing that retailers of all stripes, once left for dead, are starting to push back against Amazon , although some are having more success than others . Kroger (KR), for instance, has gained 39% during the past three months, while Target (TGT) has risen 27%, and Wal-Mart (WMT) has rallied 20%. Amazon has gained 34% during the same period. Today, it's up 1.7% to $1,316.29 at 12:35 p.m. today.
 Volatile Valeant Bounces Back While Valeant Pharmaceuticals International (VRX) has easily outperformed the S&P 500 over the past year, the specialty-pharma company suffered its worst weekly drop since August last week--a 9.7% decline that included a 2.6% drop on Friday.
None of this is new for Valeant. The stock has been quite volatile since bottomoing , hurt by downgrades and major investor skepticism , while also scoring victories like drug approvals , and pipeline progress , including the application for its latest acne treatment, submitted to the Food & Drug Administration earlier this month.
So what to make of last week's drop? Perhaps not much. Cantor Fitzgerald's Louise Chen and team argue that Valeant was hurt by worries that its traveler's diarrhea and irritable bowel syndrome treatment Xifaxan could face competition from Japan's Cosmo Pharmaceuticals (JP.3349) as early as 2019. However Chen argues that while Cosmo is expected to file for approval of a drug for traveler's diarrhea, that's an insignificant portion of Xifaxan's sales, which are much more skewed to IBS. Nor does she think that, if approved, Cosmo's drug would be used widely off-label for IBS treatment. As a result, Chen reiterated an Overweight rating and $25 price target on the stock, arguing that Friday's selloff isn't based on fundamentals.
Valeant has gained 1.4% to $21.81 at 12:28 p.m. today. The stock has gained 4.9% since the start of the year.
